newsitem.title: UK: Greenpeace settles in for long protest on oil rig.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace settles in for long protest on oil rig.

text.p: The environmental group Greenpeace hoisted a survival capsule onto a British Petroleum (BP) oil platform on Tuesday in preparation for a lengthy campaign to stop the rig reaching a new offshore field north of Scotland.
Activists boarded the Stena Dee platform on Saturday and chained themselves to it in a bid to stop the development of the Foinaven field as part of a worldwide campaign against climate change.
"The capsule will provide the activists with better protection and demonstrates we are here to stay," said Greenpeace's deputy executive director Chris Rose.
Later on Tuesday Greenpeace planned to attach solar and wind power generators to the watertight capsule.

The Stena Dee, which is said to cost BP about 100,000 pounds ($160,000) a day to hire, has hardly moved since it was boarded on the open sea and lies 16 miles (25 km) south of Foinaven and about 55 miles (88 km) northwest of the Orkney islands.
BP said it had no immediate plans to remove the activists.
"We have no plans to do anything at the moment. Our greatest desire is for Greenpeace to stop this unlawful act and leave the rig safely," a spokesman said.
He said the campaign could have unspecified knock-on effects on BP's operations at Foinaven if it were to drag on, but would not delay getting the field onstream.

So far, the protest has failed to spark much media attention in Britain, in sharp contrast with the success of a Greenpeace campaign two years ago which stopped Shell sinking the Brent Spar oil storage buoy in the Atlantic. ($ = 0.632 British Pounds)
